chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr and Safwan, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Upon the one performing Tamattu' (Umrah to Hajj) are three circumambulations of the House and two Sa'ees between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. And upon him, when he arrives in Mecca, is one circumambulation of the House, two Rak'ahs at the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and one Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. Then he shortens (his hair/nails), and this is permissible for the Umrah. And upon him, for the Hajj, are two circumambulations and one Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. And he prays two Rak'ahs at each circumambulation of the House, at the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: One performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break)
key_terms.سَعْيَانِ: Two Sa'ees (walks between Safa and Marwa)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: He shortens (referring to cutting hair or nails to exit Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific ritual requirements for Hajj al-Tamattu' according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinct ritual structure of Hajj al-Tamattu', emphasizing the separation of Umrah and Hajj rites as a key differentiator in Shia jurisprudence. It specifies that the pilgrim performs three complete sets of Tawaf and Sa'i, integrating the two Rak'ahs of prayer at Maqam Ibrahim with each circumambulation, thereby reinforcing the procedural integrity of the pilgrimage. This detailed breakdown serves as a foundational text for understanding the practical application of the Tamattu' mode of Hajj.
